healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. St. Maarten Medical Center (SMMC) is the main hospital. Healthcare is funded through social insurance (SZV) for residents. Tourists pay out-of-pocket or through travel insurance.
qualityNotes: Adequate healthcare for a small Caribbean island. SMMC provides emergency care, general surgery, and basic specialist services. Quality is reasonable for common conditions. Complex cases require evacuation to Curaçao, Colombia, or the US. Both Dutch and English widely spoken.
pharmacyHours: Mon-Fri 8am-7pm, Sat 8am-2pm. Some pharmacies open later in Philipsburg tourist area.
pharmacyTips: Several well-stocked pharmacies in Philipsburg and Simpson Bay. Common medications are available. Prices may be higher than on the mainland. Pharmacists speak English and Dutch.
prescriptionRules: Foreign prescriptions from licensed doctors are generally accepted. Controlled substances require original prescription and documentation. Dutch and US prescriptions are readily accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic painkillers
restrictedMeds.note: Opioid medications are controlled. Carry original prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. Carry documentation from prescribing physician.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring adequate supplies for your entire visit.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is strongly recommended. Specialist care may require evacuation to Curaçao or the US. Hurricane season (June-November) increases risk — ensure your policy covers weather-related emergencies.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry (unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country). Dengue and Zika virus are present — use insect repellent. Ensure routine vaccinations are current.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink. The island uses desalination plants to produce drinking water. Bottled water is also widely available.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are generally good at hotels and restaurants. Fresh seafood is excellent. Exercise normal caution with street food and ensure seafood is properly cooked.
medicalTourismNote: Not a medical tourism destination. Sint Maarten is a popular cruise and beach destination. Residents travel to Colombia, Curaçao, or the Netherlands for specialized medical procedures.
sources: Sint Maarten Ministry of Public Health
metaDescription: Health guide for Sint Maarten. Emergency numbers, hospital info, pharmacy tips, travel insurance, and vaccination advice for Caribbean travelers.

hospitals.name: St. Maarten Medical Center (SMMC)
hospitals.notes: The island's main hospital. Emergency department, general surgery, ICU, and basic specialties. English and Dutch spoken. Handles most medical emergencies for tourists.

dentalCare.availability: Several private dental practices on the island, mainly in Philipsburg and Simpson Bay.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is available and of reasonable quality. Private practices offer modern equipment. English spoken at all clinics.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private dental clinics handle emergencies during business hours. After hours, contact SMMC emergency department.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: 988 (US Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — may be accessible)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Some private practitioners available on the island
mentalHealth.notes: Limited mental health services. The Mental Health Foundation Sint Maarten provides some community-based care. English-speaking therapists available through private practice.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Moderate accessibility at major tourist facilities. Older areas and local neighborhoods have limited infrastructure.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: SMMC has wheelchair access and modern facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transportation. Taxis are the main option. Some hotel shuttle services.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Major resorts and cruise terminal areas are more accessible. Philipsburg boardwalk is wheelchair-friendly. Beaches vary in accessibility. Contact hotels in advance about specific needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at SMMC and some private clinics.
covidStatus.notes: Standard hygiene practices recommended. Healthcare capacity is limited during peak tourist season.

insuranceClaimProcess: SMMC and private clinics accept cash and major credit cards. US dollars are the official currency. Request itemized bills and medical reports. File claims with your insurer upon return.

commonCosts.note: US dollars accepted everywhere. Healthcare costs are moderate-to-high by Caribbean standards. SMMC bills in Netherlands Antillean guilders but accepts USD.

medicalEvacuation.primaryDestination: Willemstad, Curaçao or San Juan, Puerto Rico
medicalEvacuation.note: Princess Juliana International Airport handles medevac flights. Flight time to Puerto Rico or Curaçao is approximately 1-2 hours. Airport may be affected during hurricane season.
